assertions: Sir William Waller, the 1st-house / Parliamentarian side, overcomes Sir Ralph Hopton in the engagement near Alresford (Cheriton) on 29 March 1644
Sir Ralph Hopton, the 7th-house / Royalist side, is defeated and forced to give ground and retreat, not holding the field
Hopton has no supplies or assistance ready in time: only Mars and the South Node are in the 9th, so no effective support reaches him for this fight
Waller's assistance and substance are strong and effective: the Sun, lord of Waller's substance/assistants, is in the 10th in the exact degree of his exaltation, 19 degrees Aries
Hopton is personally isolated and debilitated rather than reinforced: his significator Saturn is in his fall, peregrine, sub radiis, and in no aspect to any planet
The victory for Waller is decided on the day of the engagement itself, not a drawn or indecisive encounter
summary: Waller overcomes Hopton at Cheriton on 29 March 1644; Hopton, unsupported and debilitated, is defeated and retreats.
method: Horary astrology in Lilly's tradition: 1st house, Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter and Venus for Waller versus Saturn, lord of the 7th, for Hopton, judged by essential dignity, angularity, light and aspect
reasoning: Waller's significators are dignified and supported: Moon in her exaltation with Jupiter, and Jupiter and Venus assigned to his side; the Sun, lord of his substance/assistants, is angular in the 10th at 19 Aries, the exact degree of exaltation, and the Moon is swift and increasing in light. Hopton's significator Saturn is the opposite: in his fall, peregrine, sub radiis, unaspected by any planet, and square the cusp of his own 7th, with no supplies ready (only Mars and the South Node in the 9th). Strong, assisted 1st side versus fallen, isolated 7th side gives a clear Waller victory. This is a single-day engagement question, so the time scale is the day of battle itself.
